# Report-template consistency check for next-step producer actions

## Goal / use case

Verified by the parent AC5: once the tightened `--producer-actions`
contract lands, demonstrate (via a deterministic check) that no
`skill/*/SKILL.md` final-step report template instructs or exemplifies
next-step producer actions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A grep-based consistency check (added as a pytest in a skill test
  file or as a documented command) scans every `skill/*/SKILL.md` final-step
  report template and reports ZERO next-step producer-action
  instructions/examples.
- AC2: The check's match vocabulary mirrors the shared routine-next-step
  classifier (run /skill:<name>, proceed to <stage>, "review the brief,
  then …") so it stays in sync with `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`.
- AC3: The check is offline, fast, deterministic, and needs no new runtime
  dependency.
- AC4: The check yields an unambiguous pass/fail (documented command output
  or a pytest) so the doc/template change (D1) has a clean acceptance gate.

## Key Files

- `skill/*/SKILL.md` (17 templates)
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (vocabulary source for the match patterns)
- a consistency-check test under `skill/report/tests/` or `tests/`

## Notes

Test-first: is added and run **before** the template wording change (D1).
Residual matches reported by the first run form the D1 change backlog rather
than failures of unrelated templates.
data.title: Consistency check: no next-step producer actions in templates

# Unit tests for next-step classification and renderer normalisation

## Goal / use case

Test-first coverage for parent AC2, AC3 and AC4: the shared
routine-next-step classifier in `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` and the report
renderer's producer-actions normalisation in
`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`, written before the implementations
land (F1/F2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` covers the classifier:
  "Proceed to /skill:plan", "Review the intake brief and then run
  /skill:plan" and "Next step: implement" classify as routine; "None
  needed" is unchanged; ambiguous/text-with-blocking-clauses falls back
  unchanged (all-clauses-must-match).

  "## Producer Actions" section reads exactly "None needed" for

  remediation list in comment #4") are rendered unchanged (no over-eager

- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`

## Summary

The implement and intake skills claim work items by setting the assignee (the
agent identity) and `status=in_progress` at the start of their run. When the
run reaches ANY terminal outcome — success, failure, or abort — the assignee
is never cleared. Under the assignee-hold convention (AGENTS_GLOBAL: "non-empty
assignee = scheduling hold (producer `Map`; clear to release)") a lingering
assignee holds the item and blocks re-dispatch/re-pickup.

The audit skill already clears the assignee on terminal verdicts
(SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS); implement and intake must mirror that behaviour:
every terminal outcome clears the assignee so the item is released for the
producer and the next lifecycle step.

## User Story

As a dispatcher/producer, I need the implement and intake skills to clear the
assignee at the end of every run (success, failure, or abort) so completed or
released work items are never left on a scheduling hold.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — shared `StatusLifecycle` context manager
  (opt-in `clear_assignee_on_exit=True` clears the assignee on the successful
  `completed` transition; default `False` keeps other skills unchanged. The
  failure path still clears the assignee only when constructed with
  `assignee=`)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start` (claim, failure
  resets), `phase_finish` (success via `StatusLifecycle` + failure resets),
  `phase_abort` (reset to `open`)
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — `cmd_start` (claim), `cmd_finish`,
  `cmd_auto_complete`, `cmd_abort`, failure resets
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — document the
  clear-on-completion behaviour
- Tests: `skill/implement/tests/` (incl. `test_phase_abort_clears_assignee.py`,
  `test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `test_phase_start_claim.py`),
  `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py`,
  `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py`, and the parent-advance assertions in
  `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` / `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `implement.py finish` success path clears the assignee while still
      advancing status to `completed` / stage `in_review`
- [ ] Every `implement.py` failure reset (start/finish) and `phase_abort`
      clears the assignee together with the reset to `open`
- [ ] `intake.py finish`, `auto-complete`, and `abort` each clear the assignee
      (and failure resets do too)
- [ ] The shared `StatusLifecycle` supports opt-in clear-on-success so other
      skills are unaffected unless they request it (no silent behaviour change)
- [ ] Both `SKILL.md` files document that completion clears the assignee
      regardless of outcome
- [ ] Regression tests cover success and failure/abort outcomes for both
      skills; all tests pass
- [ ] Full project test suite passes at the dev-push gate

## Assumptions

- "Regardless of the state of the completion" = every terminal outcome
  (success → `in_review`, failure/abort → `open`) clears the assignee.
- Assignee clearing is applied only where the skill itself owns the
  transitional update (final `completed`/`open` writes), not to arbitrary
  comments or intermediate updates.
data.title: implement/intake: clear assignee on completion regardless of outcome

# Audit runner must not re-flag a previously reviewed item on a passing release-time audit

## Background

On 2026-10-27 a `dev`→`main` release of the ContextHub store was attempted. The
producer had already reviewed and cleared `needsProducerReview` on 14 top-level
`in_review` items. The release's audit remediation (the gate's own
auto-remediation, `--refresh-audits`, and batch drains) then re-audited those
same items; every re-audit passed, and each pass **unconditionally re-armed**
`needsProducerReview = yes`. The release gate consequently reported 14 items
"awaiting producer review" — items the producer had already reviewed. The
review was silently discarded.

Root cause (SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, passing-verdict
lifecycle, ~line 13576–13583):

```python
cmd = ["wl", "update", ctx.issue_id]
if ctx.original_stage == "done":
    cmd += ["--status", "completed"]
else:
    cmd += ["--status", "completed", "--stage", "in_review"]
cmd += ["--assignee", ""]
if not ctx.wi or not ctx.wi.get("parentId"):
    cmd += ["--needs-producer-review", "yes"]   # <-- unconditional for top-level items
```

There is no check for whether the producer already reviewed the item. The
`work_items.needsProducerReview` column (ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts`)
is a bare `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`: `false` cannot distinguish
*"producer reviewed and cleared"* from *"never flagged yet"*, and
`wl reviewed <id> false` is a flag-only flip that bumps no timestamp
(`docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`: "Flag-only flips of `needsProducerReview` do not bump
`updatedAt`"). So the review state is unobservable after the fact and any
re-audit overwrites it.

Conversely, the failing-verdict path only flags for producer review when
`ctx.merge_gate_blocker` is set (~line 13643); an ordinary `Ready to close: No`
leaves `needsProducerReview=false`, so genuinely failing items never reach the
producer-review queue.

History: the current unconditional-on-pass behaviour was introduced by
SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5 (set on 'yes' verdicts) and narrowed to top-level items by
SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H; SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW introduced "set producerReview flag
when an automated audit marks the item ready to close". This item refines that
contract rather than reverting it.

## Target outcome

A producer review survives a subsequent passing release-time audit, while a
failing release-time audit always routes the item to producer review.

- **Passing audit (`Ready to close: Yes`) on a top-level item:**
  - if the producer has already reviewed this item (see *Review-state signal*
    below), leave `needsProducerReview` as-is (`false`) — do **not** re-flag;
  - if the item has never been reviewed, flag `needsProducerReview = yes`
    (current behaviour preserved — first pass still enters the review queue).
- **Failing audit (`Ready to close: No`) on any top-level item:** set
  `needsProducerReview = yes` (generalise the existing merge-gate-blocker
  branch), and never clear an existing review silently.
- **Children:** unchanged — child items are covered by their parent's audit and
  are not flagged (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A passing verdict on a top-level item whose producer has already reviewed it does not set `needsProducerReview = yes`; the existing `false` value is preserved and the item is not re-entered into the producer-review queue.
- A passing verdict on a top-level item that has never been reviewed still sets `needsProducerReview = yes` (first-pass review queue behaviour unchanged).
- A failing verdict (`Ready to close: No`) on a top-level item sets `needsProducerReview = yes` regardless of whether `merge_gate_blocker` is set, so genuinely failing items are always surfaced to the producer.
- The review-state signal is durable and auditable: it distinguishes "reviewed and cleared" from "never flagged", and it is invalidated when the item's reviewed content changes (a materially changed item requires a fresh producer review).
- Regression tests cover all four transitions (never-reviewed pass -> flagged; reviewed pass -> preserved; fail -> flagged; review-then-content-change pass -> flagged again) and run in the default suite.
- No behavioural change for child items: a passing verdict on a child never sets `needsProducerReview`.
- The audit runner's existing lifecycle guarantees are preserved: pre-audit status/stage restore on abort and on infrastructure failure, `updatedAt = auditedAt` on audit persist, and the assignee clear-on-terminal behaviour.
- Docs updated so the pass/fail flag semantics are explicit (audit skill reference and/or `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`), including that producer review is content-scoped.

## Review-state signal — design options

`needsProducerReview` alone cannot answer "was this reviewed?". Choose one:

- **Option A (preferred) — durable marker.** Add a review marker written by
  `wl reviewed <id> false` (e.g. `producerReviewedAt` plus the item's audit
  content fingerprint at review time, either on `work_items` or in
  `audit_results`). The audit runner compares the stored reviewed fingerprint
  with the new audit fingerprint: equal -> preserve `false`; different/absent ->
  flag `yes`. This is precise and content-scoped, but is a ContextHub worklog
  schema + CLI change (see Dependencies).
- **Option B (no schema change) — infer from the existing invariant.** Only a
  passing audit sets the flag, so a top-level item that currently has
  `needsProducerReview == false`, `stage == in_review`, and a *prior passing*
  audit can only have been cleared by a producer (or the ship close-step
  override). The runner preserves `false` in that case and flags `yes`
  otherwise (no prior audit, or prior audit failed). Simple, but cannot detect
  content drift since the review — combine with the audit freshness check
  (`content fingerprint unchanged`) to bound that gap.

Record the chosen option in the item before implementing.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — passing-verdict lifecycle (~13576–13583) and failing-verdict lifecycle (~13626–13644); the place both rules change.
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — audit persistence (auditedAt / fingerprint).
- ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts` — `needsProducerReview` column and the `work_items` schema (only if Option A).
- ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed*.ts` (or equivalent `wl reviewed` handler) — where a review marker would be written (only if Option A).
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — flag semantics and the "flag-only flips do not bump `updatedAt`" contract.
- Audit skill reference docs (`docs/dev/audit-*`) — document content-scoped producer review.

## Dependencies

- Option A requires a ContextHub (worklog) change: a durable review marker and
  its `wl` CLI/API surface. Raise a ContextHub work item and block this item on
  it if Option A is chosen. Option B needs no cross-repo change.

## Evidence (reproduction)

1. Create a top-level item, audit it to a passing verdict -> `needsProducerReview = yes`.
2. `wl reviewed <id> false` -> flag clears.
3. Re-audit the unchanged item to a passing verdict (or run the ship gate's
   `--refresh-audits`) -> observed: `needsProducerReview` flips back to `yes`
   with `updatedAt == auditedAt`. Expected after fix: stays `false`.

Observed on 2026-10-27 for WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P, WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8,
WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6, WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66, WL-0MVMSE2S0006L56D, WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0,
WL-0MVMSE5LN003KCPQ, WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX, WL-0MVOTIJ2U000JI44,
WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG, WL-0MVPRZU0A000TSWD, WL-0MVM92MZ50075E6B.

<!-- discovered-from: ContextHub release attempt 2026-10-27 (dev→main blocked by spurious producer-review flags) -->
data.title: Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review

Auto-plan completed with review: effort Extra Small / risk Low — below the planning threshold, so no decomposition was created. Implementation commit `2d21f1485` is already merged on `dev` (branch `wl-SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM-...`), so planning verified the existing content against the shipped code.

**Review summary per stage**

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — Summary, User Story and the 7 ACs trace cleanly: success path (AC1), failure/abort resets (AC2), intake terminal commands (AC3), opt-in `StatusLifecycle` flag (AC4), docs (AC5), regression tests (AC6), suite gate (AC7). Referenced precedent SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS exists and is completed. No invented or contradictory ACs.
2. **Completeness** — description/goal/ACs/assumptions all present; all six named Key Files exist. Two accuracy gaps fixed: the `status_lifecycle.py` bullet still described the pre-change behaviour (no clear-on-success) and the Tests bullet omitted the files actually touched by the merged commit. `validate_key_files_format()` reports no syntactic issues.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — no children, so no dependency edges; test-first ordering is expressed in the AC order (AC6 tests before AC7 suite gate). No change needed.
4. **Scope sizing** — single small vertical slice (code + tests + docs) confirmed by Extra Small / Low risk; decomposition would add overhead, so the skip decision is documented rather than phasing the item.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every AC is binary-verifiable: `test_clear_assignee_on_success_exit`, `test_assignee_cleared_on_failure`, `test_assignee_on_entry` (proves the default is unaffected), `test_phase_abort_clears_assignee`, `test_finish_no_diff_status`, `test_intake_scripts_cwd` assignee assertions, plus the SKILL.md statements and the dev-push gate evidence.
6. **Polish & handoff** — description is clear, UK English, actionable; assumptions (all terminal outcomes clear the assignee; only skill-owned terminal writes are affected) are recorded and match the implementation.

**AC coverage review:** `proceed` — 7 parent ACs, 100% covered by the completed implementation (no children required). Stage advanced to `plan_complete`; assignee released.
